Readable-numeral decision: tabular numerals for the 2 numeric readout item(s).

Type-role contract: the screen name takes the title role, the decision context takes the subtitle, each information item takes its natural role (eyebrow for metadata, label for chrome-ish captions, body for prose, code for identifiers), and status states take the label role at legible size.

Acceptance criteria declared: no label below 11px; uppercase reserved for eyebrows; one spacing rhythm step between sibling regions; body columns around 75 characters. Measured on rendered evidence when screenshot critique runs (issue #22 phase 2).

rejectedAlternatives.reason: Outranked on the weighted total (7.04 vs 7.24). arranging or locating things is itself the task, so the composition has to be a place rather than a list (topology decision, shard links between clusters,bandwidth per link,drop rate per path,node pressure by resource,route healthy vs struggling,cluster traffic share,last rebalance on each cluster item(s)). taskFit: 9 — ranked affinity for the 'topology' decision class, plus the brief's stated relationships that this family draws. relationshipClarity: 9 — 4 stated relationship item(s): 'shard links between clusters', 'bandwidth per link', 'node pressure by resource' — drawn, not listed. informationHierarchy: 8 — 7 information item(s) against a spatial field: dense past ~8 nodes, individual labels stop being readable in place. densityScanability: 6 — how 7 item(s) sit in this family: spaced nodes need room per label.

Outranked on the weighted total (5.72 vs 7.24). an instrument keeps the state of the whole at eye level and the object under it, so intervention happens where the evidence is (topology decision, shard links between clusters,bandwidth per link,drop rate per path,node pressure by resource,route healthy vs struggling,cluster traffic share,last rebalance on each cluster item(s)). taskFit: 6 — ranked affinity for the 'topology' decision class. informationHierarchy: 9 — 7 information item(s) against a family that packs them into comparable columns and rows. densityScanability: 7 — how 7 item(s) sit in this family: rows/columns absorb inventory.

Outranked on the weighted total (5.52 vs 7.24). an inventory of comparable things reads fastest as rows, which is the shape a listing already has (topology decision, shard links between clusters,bandwidth per link,drop rate per path,node pressure by resource,route healthy vs struggling,cluster traffic share,last rebalance on each cluster item(s)). taskFit: 5 — ranked affinity for the 'topology' decision class. informationHierarchy: 9 — 7 information item(s) against a family that packs them into comparable columns and rows. densityScanability: 7 — how 7 item(s) sit in this family: rows/columns absorb inventory.

Outranked on the weighted total (5.52 vs 7.24). a story over time must keep its order visible; a grid erases exactly what the brief is about (topology decision, shard links between clusters,bandwidth per link,drop rate per path,node pressure by resource,route healthy vs struggling,cluster traffic share,last rebalance on each cluster item(s)). taskFit: 5 — ranked affinity for the 'topology' decision class. informationHierarchy: 9 — 7 information item(s) against a family that packs them into comparable columns and rows. densityScanability: 7 — how 7 item(s) sit in this family: rows/columns absorb inventory.
